title: Minimum linear arrangement

problem.name: Minimum linear arrangement
problem.statement_latex:
For $G=(V,E)$, compute $\min_\pi\sum_{uv\in E}|\pi(u)-\pi(v)|$ over bijections $\pi:V\to[n]$. The sum measures total edge length in a linear layout and models total wiring length or aggregate communication distance.
The quantum comparison uses QRAM time and the classical comparison uses RAM operations on the graph.
problem.statement_text: For $G=(V,E)$, compute $\min_\pi\sum_{uv\in E}|\pi(u)-\pi(v)|$ over bijections $\pi:V\to[n]$. The sum measures total edge length in a linear layout and models total wiring length or aggregate communication distance. The quantum comparison uses QRAM time and the classical comparison uses RAM operations on the graph.

quantum.details_latex: The sum of edge lengths equals the sum of cut sizes over the prefixes of the ordering. This additive objective fits the ordering recurrence, with polynomial-time evaluation of each transition. The quantum algorithm uses nested minimum finding and coherent access to partially precomputed subset values.
quantum.details_text: The sum of edge lengths equals the sum of cut sizes over the prefixes of the ordering. This additive objective fits the ordering recurrence, with polynomial-time evaluation of each transition. The quantum algorithm uses nested minimum finding and coherent access to partially precomputed subset values.

classical.details_latex: For each subset, the recurrence minimizes its accumulated prefix-cut cost over choices of the last vertex. Straightforward implementations include an $O(m2^n)$ bound, with polynomial factors depending on the graph representation, and use exponential memory. Specialized graph classes, including trees, admit faster classical algorithms and are separate input regimes.

strength.description_latex: Polynomial speedup through a smaller exponential constant, obtained from amplitude amplification and quantum minimum finding.

hardware.description_latex: A subset needs $n$ active qubits and the objective needs $O(\log(nm))$ bits, with reversible workspace and exponential coherent table storage. Fault tolerance is needed for useful depths.
